MALARIA.title: Malaria (mosquito-borne parasite infection)

items: Malaria is an infection with a parasite that is spread by mosquito bites.
Symptoms can start 7 to 30 days after a bite, and sometimes months later for some types.
Fever that may come in cycles, with shivering (rigors) and sweating.
Headache, body aches, and an enlarged spleen in some people.
Blood film, thick and thin, to look for the parasite. Malaria is confirmed by a test, not by symptoms alone.
A rapid antigen test (RDT), which can be positive for weeks after treatment.
Blood count, kidney and liver tests, blood glucose, and lactate if you are unwell.
Your doctor will choose the antimalarial treatment based on the species and how severe the illness is.
Malaria is treated with antimalarial medicine, not antibiotics.

sections.h: What you can do at home
items: Use mosquito nets and repellent, especially at night.
Tell your doctor about any recent travel to a malaria area.
Some types can come back months later. Keep your follow-up appointments.
This leaflet gives general information. Follow your doctor's advice.

urgent: The source entry lists no specific emergency sign for this condition.
Get urgent help if you feel suddenly much worse, or are confused or drowsy.
